steps.message:
`client.py` is shared, not staging-only. `scripts/export_prod.py` imports the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports` and points `REPORTS_BASE_URL` at `https://reports.example.com`. So `verify=False` on those two calls in `client.py:11` and `client.py:17` turns off TLS certificate validation for the **production** nightly finance export as well — that traffic becomes vulnerable to an active man-in-the-middle (any interceptor can present any cert, read the report data, and alter responses), silently and with no error. `urllib3` will also start emitting `InsecureRequestWarning` on every prod run.

The "it's just staging" part is true of the *intent* but not of the *code* as written, so I want a yes before touching it.

questions.question: client.py is shared with the production export. How should I scope the TLS change?

options.label: Staging only, via env flag
options.description: Add something like REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS (default true) and pass it as verify= on both calls. sync_staging.py sets it false; export_prod.py keeps full verification. Smallest change that does not weaken prod.

options.label: Trust the staging cert
options.description: Keep verify on everywhere, but point it at the staging self-signed cert/CA file (verify=<path>) when hitting staging. Strongest option; needs the cert file available to whoever runs the script.

options.label: verify=False unconditionally
options.description: Exactly what you asked: hardcode verify=False on both requests calls in client.py. Accepts that the production nightly export also stops validating certificates.

Done. Both `requests.get` calls in `client.py` now pass `verify=False`.

Two things to be aware of, since you chose the unconditional form:

- **Production is affected.** `scripts/export_prod.py` uses these same functions against `https://reports.example.com`, so the nightly finance export no longer validates certificates either.
- **Expect warnings.** `urllib3` will print `InsecureRequestWarning` on every call from both scripts. I didn't suppress them — silencing the warning would remove the only remaining signal that verification is off. Say the word if you want them muted.
